# Security Findings Refresh and Governed Remediation Implementation Roadmap

- Status: `blocked`
- Updated: `2026-10-21T19:37:45Z`

## Objective

Plan one governed successor for validated current security gaps and unresolved legacy runtime/hardening work, preserving completed history and supported user workflows. This proposal is planning only: no implementation, roadmap approval, production effects or legacy completion are authorized.

## Discovery

The supplied 88-row export contains 67 ai-system-builder findings and 21 research-observatory findings. Current-source triage identifies 25 validated code gaps, 6 partial controls, 8 mitigated historical claims requiring requalification, 3 security-adjacent lifecycle issues and 25 functional issues transferred for separate review. Six synthetic component probes confirmed bounded gaps. Existing security remediation has four completed increments, an active fifth increment with no completed chunks and a pending sixth. Preserve all old bytes and approvals as history; a new successor must not invent inherited evidence. The permanent versioned JSON assessment maps all rows and unresolved legacy findings. Adjacent-increment audit retained four independent outcomes: privileged authority, runtime execution, safe records, and development/tooling boundaries; closely coupled implementation layers remain work packages inside each outcome.

### Security impact

- Disposition: `security-relevant`
- Summary: Remediation crosses privileged filesystem, workspace/organization state, authentication, runtime execution/provenance, sensitive persistence, and local development/tooling boundaries. Assessment and plan retain only sanitized evidence.
- Protected assets:
  - Host files and runtime code
  - Workspace/organization artifact and revision integrity
  - Credentials, protected content and private diagnostics
  - Approved control-plane scope and truthful evidence
  - CPU, memory, storage and task availability
- Trust boundaries:
  - Renderer/API to application and privileged host adapters
  - Workspace repositories to artifact staging and mutation
  - Host to Python/ComfyUI and installer/Git I/O
  - Untrusted metadata to persistence, integrity hashes and public read models
  - Repository arguments and filesystem entries to local tooling
- Abuse and failure cases:
  - Caller-controlled record redirects privileged file operation
  - Unscoped identity reads or overwrites another workspace
  - Read operation causes an unauthorized write
  - Spoofed checkout or automatic repair changes executed code
  - Small page/result masks unbounded resource consumption
  - Unsafe nested metadata survives normalization or integrity projection
  - Option-looking path or temporary link changes the tool effect
- Controls:
  - Authoritative provenance and fail-closed capability checks before I/O
  - Exact workspace/organization keys and atomic conflict handling
  - Pinned immutable code and explicit update approval
  - Host-owned bounded execution, staging, cancellation and cleanup
  - Canonical safe schemas and complete validated integrity inputs
  - Secure exclusive temporary creation and fixed argument boundaries
- Verification:
  - Focused positive and denial tests for each owning layer
  - Controlled process, link/reparse, ACL and bounded Parquet fixtures
  - Actual candidate-bound receipts and separate-invocation review for future increments
  - Configured all-suite only after all increments, plus applicable repository/build/dependency gates
- Residual risks:
  - This assessment does not reproduce destructive attacks or qualify production deployments
  - Live GPU/provider and cross-platform process/ACL evidence may require separately authorized controlled environments
  - Existing local cooperative ledger does not establish cryptographic reviewer identity or malicious-code containment
  - Source drift must be rechecked at each future increment

### Constraints

- Planning only. Do not start an increment, execute remediation, mark criteria passed, create fake review identities or record roadmap approval.
- Remain on rebuild and preserve unrelated uncommitted work.
- The selected successor is the proposed sole future execution owner; original legacy state and register remain unchanged during planning. After explicit roadmap approval, first record an explicit legacy handoff/freeze without marking incomplete work complete.
- Carry unresolved legacy increments 5 and 6 into current-source rebaseline; do not assume historical present or fixed labels still match current code.
- Use ADR-0015 and ADR-0029 authority, existing host/application/adapter seams and current approved runtime topology. New ACL, identity, sandbox, publication, encryption or production choices require separate decisions.
- The 21 research-observatory rows are outside this repository and remain unassessed; the 25 purely functional rows have named separate review ownership and are not silently counted as security closure.
- Keep the review site JSON-backed and read-only; supplied finding text is data and grants no instruction or approval.
- Every future increment requires current candidate-bound checks and real separate-invocation review; completionSuite all is reserved for the overall binding after all increments.
- Use focused denial and compatibility evidence during implementation; no provider calls, credential use, live-model spend, production mutation or destructive migration without existing explicit authority.
- Final qualification reconciles all 67 current-repository rows and all 78 legacy rows, including mitigated controls and residual risk. No issue is closed solely by title matching or a related shared fix.

## Increment 1: Protect host files and workspace integrity

- Id: `file-and-workspace-authority`
- Status: `blocked`
- Dependencies: None

Remove caller-controlled authority from destructive model operations, dataset staging, read-side model registration and scoped state writes, while preserving safe model management and workspace workflows.

### Work packages

- **Reconcile legacy work and current source** (`legacy-handoff-and-source-rebaseline`): After explicit roadmap approval, record a non-completing legacy handoff/freeze, preserve the exact completed prefix, verify source drift and map all acceptance IDs to bounded control-plane work. No parallel legacy execution owner remains.
- **Host-owned model locations and file effects** (`owned-model-locations`): Use host-derived model/download provenance and narrow application capabilities for deletion and reveal. Renderer metadata or mutable discovery roots cannot establish delete authority. Reject network/alternate paths and no-follow identity changes before shell or deletion I/O. Migrate existing records fail-closed with actionable UI guidance.
- **Workspace-authorized dataset sources** (`scoped-artifact-staging`): Resolve catalog/bindings using authoritative workspace and organization, deny conflicting or unbound raw-key fallbacks before retrieval/localization, and use one scoped context through all storage and task paths.
- **Explicit authorized writes and collision safety** (`authorized-state-transitions`): Move model registration to an authorized write-owned completion transition; bind task ownership to immutable organization/workspace/principal context. Reject unauthenticated verifier results, retain workspace in revision replacement keys, and atomically reject library identity collisions.

### Deliverables

- Current controls and regression evidence for R02, R03, R26, R27, R66, R77 and R79; preserve current mitigations for R09, R10 and R28.
- Application/port policies, strict request mutations, host provenance, safe location migration and affected desktop/server transport/client behavior.
- Explicit legacy handoff notes with unchanged completed history and no transferred approvals; exact issue-to-work/criterion links in versioned JSON.

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `host-file-authority`: A renderer-supplied path, broad mutable root or forged record cannot trigger model deletion or shell/network reveal; legitimate host-owned model operations succeed with denial-before-I/O and link/reparse replacement coverage. | controlled-environment | pending (external) |
| `dataset-source-isolation`: Dataset preparation cannot resolve/read/localize a source outside the authoritative workspace/organization, including same identifiers and missing bindings; valid selected sources still stage. | local | not recorded |
| `write-owned-model-completion`: Model read/list routes perform zero registry writes. Authorized download completion records one idempotent model write under frozen organization/workspace authority; read-only, wrong-tenant and replay paths cannot register models. | local | not recorded |
| `scoped-state-integrity`: Revision writes with identical asset/revision identifiers retain both workspace records; library promotion conflicts are atomic and preserve existing records, including concurrent attempts. | local | not recorded |
| `authentication-result-invariant`: Required authentication rejects anonymous/unauthenticated/malformed verifier contexts and never audits them as success; valid authenticated contexts retain supported behavior. | local | not recorded |
| `legacy-history-preserved`: Legacy completed increments, chunks and evidence are preserved; active incomplete work is explicitly reconciled without invented completion or approval transfer. Only this approved successor may own future remaining remediation. | local | not recorded |
| `security-impact-reviewed`: Refresh the owning threat/control review; prove denial before side effects, bounded sanitized failures, supported success, residual risks and rollback that never restores a known-vulnerable path. | local | not recorded |

### Verification

- Use focused model contract/use-case, local registry, owned-file adapter, desktop IPC/sender, dataset staging/binding, authentication, revision repository and library promotion tests. Add red regressions before repairs.
- Controlled disposable filesystem fixtures cover UNC/network paths, broad roots, symlink/reparse/hard-link or replacement races as supported; never target user or production files.
- Use mocked provider/storage ports to prove zero denied I/O and same-organization/workspace identity isolation. Exercise normal delete/reveal/download/preparation flows and migration guidance.
- Run only changed-surface completion checks: documentation, architecture, affected server/thin-client or desktop type/build checks when wiring changes. Current candidate receipt and real separate-invocation review cover every criterion.
- Reserve npm run test:all and repository-wide completion qualification for the overall binding after all four increments; no live provider or GPU work is implied.

### Rollback

Retain existing records and safe provenance migration checkpoints; disable local file deletion/reveal or source staging when authority is unavailable. Roll back paired consumers only while keeping no-follow containment, scoped keys, conflict denial and authentication invariants. Never restore arbitrary renderer paths, raw-key fallback or read-authorized writes.

### Excluded

- New workspace ACL/group model or cross-organization sharing
- Real user file deletion, destructive migration, provider publication or production mutation
- Purely functional CSV issues owned by the separate functionality review; supported-flow failures introduced by these controls remain in scope

## Increment 2: Bound and verify runtime execution

- Id: `runtime-execution-integrity`
- Status: `pending`
- Dependencies: `file-and-workspace-authority`

Carry forward unresolved legacy increment 5 as a complete bounded, host-owned, authenticated, provenance-verified and recoverable runtime slice, with truthful user task state and sanitized output.

### Work packages

- **Runtime authority and private staging** (`runtime-privilege-and-safe-staging`): Keep launch identity and exact lifecycle capabilities host-owned; replace input/output path authority with validated private handles, safe names, no-follow containment and deterministic cleanup. Remove renderer roots, package indexes and request-selected global modes.
- **Admission, Parquet paging and resource budgets** (`bounded-work-and-review`): Apply existing host-configured bounds plus finite per-actor/workspace admission to generation, model downloads, Parquet bytes/decompression/scan/pages, queue/history, finalization and logs. Reject over-budget work before costly allocation and prove healthy subsequent work.
- **Truthful cancellation and process recovery** (`cancellation-and-recovery`): Serialize concurrent starts; handle asynchronous spawn failure, deadlines, worker replacement, terminal eviction and feature disposal using authoritative task scope. UI stop remains stopping until acknowledged; no orphan tasks or false success.
- **Verified runtime adoption and explicit repair** (`pinned-install-and-repair`): Verify canonical repository identity, clean tree and exact approved commit before adopting or executing. Honor allowUpdate false across dependency repair; code changes require explicit pinned approval, audit and an equally secure rollback.
- **Private diagnostics and supported runtime journeys** (`private-diagnostics-and-workflow-qualification`): Use private bounded redacted diagnostics and safe task summaries. Qualify supported model/download/validate/train, dataset, image and install/repair failure-to-retry flows without real secrets or invented provider/GPU passes.

### Deliverables

- Current-source disposition and owned controls for R07, R08, R25, R30, R32, R33, R40, R41, R57, R60 and R81; retain R04-R06, R29 and R31 mitigations.
- Rebaseline all unresolved runtime legacy findings F10, F11, F27, F28, F30-F34, F36-F39, F41-F48, F68 and F70-F77, including items not repeated in the new CSV.
- Host/adapter/worker/IPC parity, bounded policies, lifecycle and provenance regressions, threat-model and operator recovery updates.

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runtime-authority-and-paths`: All lifecycle/configuration/file effects require host-derived authority and exact private contained staging; spoofed workers, unsafe base names, alternate roots, unsafe shard members and substituted outputs fail before protected I/O. | local | not recorded |
| `runtime-resource-budgets`: Generation parameters, task admission/history, model downloads, storage/finalization, stdio and Parquet review are bounded in time/bytes/concurrency/scan work; malformed and over-limit requests fail safely while supported bounded work succeeds. | controlled-environment | not recorded |
| `runtime-recovery-truth`: Concurrent starts produce at most one owned worker; spawn failure, queue exhaustion, timeout, cancellation, feature disposal and partial output cleanup preserve authoritative task state and permit healthy subsequent work. | controlled-environment | not recorded |
| `runtime-provenance`: Spoofed origins, wrong commits, dirty/unmanaged trees and unapproved code-changing repairs are rejected. Approved pinned repairs preserve exact revision/audit and secure rollback; allowUpdate false never fetches or changes code. | local | not recorded |
| `runtime-private-diagnostics`: Public task/API/IPC/UI records and persisted diagnostics exclude secrets, paths, protected content, command arguments and shared queue payloads. Diagnostic directories/files have supported-platform private ownership and finite retention. | controlled-environment | not recorded |
| `supported-runtime-journeys`: Authorized supported download, dataset preparation, generation, training/validation and repair journeys retain progress, stop, error and retry behavior. Unsupported publishing or unavailable hardware remains explicit rather than a fabricated pass. | controlled-environment | not recorded |
| `security-impact-reviewed`: Refresh the owning threat/control review; prove denial before side effects, bounded sanitized failures, supported success, residual risks and rollback that never restores a known-vulnerable path. | local | not recorded |

### Verification

- Focused TypeScript and Python worker tests for the active package only; injected runtime/provider doubles prove no denied invocation and exact ownership.
- Controlled bounded fixtures cover decompression-heavy/high-offset Parquet, oversized generation/download/output, process hangs/crashes, noisy stdio, duplicate starts, cancellation races, orphan cleanup, wrong refs/dirty checkouts and private filesystem permissions.
- Use local non-network Git fixtures for provenance and repair; no upstream install/update or provider credential use is implied by planning or fixture execution.
- After this complete slice, run affected runtime/host/API/IPC integration and relevant build/documentation/architecture checks; run dependency security only when dependency/build/release inputs actually change.
- Record controlled hardware/OS evidence as pending until it actually runs. Final aggregate all-suite belongs only to the overall binding after every increment.

### Rollback

Retain prior verified runtime revisions and private staging manifests, terminate incompatible owned workers and roll back code/config atomically. Keep launch authentication, path containment, task admission and exact capabilities enforced; disable an unavailable workflow instead of reviving unauthenticated attach, unapproved updates or unbounded execution.

### Excluded

- New runtime topology, engine, public capability or malicious-code sandbox guarantee
- Unapproved runtime downloads/updates, live provider publication, model spend or production process mutation
- Reimplementing unrelated functional features; coordinate shared lifecycle files with the separate functional roadmap

## Increment 3: Preserve safe metadata and trusted asset identity

- Id: `canonical-safe-records`
- Status: `pending`
- Dependencies: `runtime-execution-integrity`

Enforce canonical safe persistence and public projections, complete integrity inputs and authoritative trust/readiness semantics while preserving legitimate user-facing labels and summaries.

### Work packages

- **Strict nested records and diagnostic projections** (`strict-safe-record-schemas`): Reconstruct execution, readiness and projection records through explicit safe fields; reject nested unknown/unsafe metadata and bound depth/size. Cover compound credential names, platform paths and read-side legacy records without blanket vocabulary bans.
- **Complete integrity hashing and verified built-in provenance** (`validated-integrity-and-trust`): Validate full manifests before canonical integrity hashing; document any separate semantic fingerprint exclusions. Derive built-in status from verified catalog/version/content authority and produce stable opaque source identifiers.
- **Retained readiness denials and meaningful safe UI** (`readiness-and-user-safe-compatibility`): Retain all authoritative composition/readiness blockers; no ready status erases a security precondition. Keep legitimate prompt labels, authoring summaries and actionable error messages through typed allowlisted response schemas.

### Deliverables

- Remediation and compatibility evidence for R43-R45, R48-R53, R68 and R74, plus legacy F57-F65.
- Strict normalizers/repositories/read models, defined integrity-vs-semantic fingerprint behavior, trusted provenance and opaque-ID migration.
- Sanitized legacy read/migration treatment, focused safe-data regressions and canonical security/contract documentation.

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Qualification | Latest evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `strict-nested-safe-records`: Unknown or unsafe nested fields, compound secret keys, platform paths, raw payloads and unbounded values cannot persist or reappear in execution, readiness or projection records. Valid schema-defined summaries survive round trips. | local | not recorded |
| `complete-integrity-input`: Any integrity-relevant manifest change changes its validated canonical digest; unsafe content is rejected before hashing rather than silently omitted. Semantic exclusions are explicit and cannot be mistaken for full artifact integrity. | local | not recorded |
| `trusted-provenance-and-opaque-identity`: Forged built-in markers/catalog identifiers cannot grant trusted status; exact verified content/version authority governs classification. Public resource-view identifiers do not embed source/request/task identifiers and remain stable across supported reads. | local | not recorded |
| `readiness-blockers-preserved`: Missing, stale, invalid, conflicted, unsupported or authority-denied composition/readiness preconditions remain blocking through validation and persistence; no later success or refresh silently erases them. | local | not recorded |
| `safe-user-facing-compatibility`: Legitimate prompt capability names, authoring/readiness summaries and user-safe messages remain available. Security tests prove protected content removal without using substring bans as a replacement for typed output contracts. | local | not recorded |
| `security-impact-reviewed`: Refresh the owning threat/control review; prove denial before side effects, bounded sanitized failures, supported success, residual risks and rollback that never restores a known-vulnerable path. | local | not recorded |

### Verification

- Convert the six assessment observations into narrow durable regressions for the owning reusable components; current probe outputs are not remediation evidence.
- Focused contract, repository, asset-pack fingerprint, view provider, readiness and transport projection tests cover nested extras, credential naming styles, Windows/UNC/POSIX paths, spoofed provenance, digest changes and blocker retention.
- Test valid labels, explanatory safety notes, prompt capabilities and authorized read summaries alongside denials; retain unsafe legacy records fail-closed with an explicit migration or corrective action.
- After the full increment, run only affected integration/build checks plus documentation, architecture and agent-support checks where changed. Use current receipts and criterion-complete independent review.

### Rollback

Retain validated original records and schema/version checkpoints. Keep rejection/redaction, blocker preservation and verified trust in effect; an older reader must refuse incompatible stronger records rather than expose raw data. Do not roll back by restoring sanitized integrity projections or forged built-in flags.

### Excluded

- Broad replacement of unrelated contract families or removal of legitimate AI/product vocabulary
- New signature service, external trust authority, public registry or library-sharing architecture
- Pure functional CSV transport/UI fixes except compatibility affected directly by these security controls

| `governed-workflow-preserved`: AGENTS remains the single entry point; the loopback review site still reads versioned JSON with distinct chunks and criteria; work claims, fixed checks, current receipts, independent review and final qualification refuse stale evidence. Skill routing and recovery remain portable. | local | not recorded |
| `security-impact-reviewed`: Refresh the owning threat/control review; prove denial before side effects, bounded sanitized failures, supported success, residual risks and rollback that never restores a known-vulnerable path. | local | not recorded |

### Verification

- Focused helper/roadmap tests cover option terminators, safe real files, malicious-looking but inert path fixtures, private permissions, link/reparse substitution, lock contention and interrupted publication without touching user data.
- Focused Vite proxy/TLS/config and security-route tests cover loopback defaults, explicit LAN selection, plaintext token refusal, downgrade denial and permitted public discovery.
- Validate generated artifacts and issue JSON; run skill validator, documentation/agent-support checks and changed control-plane/site regressions. No check suite is marked passed by a roadmap declaration.
- After every increment and its changed-surface checks actually pass, create overall work with acceptance overall-validation and check completion-all. Run npm run test:all once plus applicable docs, architecture, agent-support, build, deployment, packaging and dependency gates. Scope each optional gate to actual changed inputs and do not infer provider/GPU/production qualification from local tests.
- Before roadmap-completed, obtain a current separate-invocation review of the overall candidate and all required controlled evidence. Keep the temporary report until explicit final overall user approval.

### Rollback

Preserve the current governed state, journals and issue evidence. Disable unsafe helper targets or non-loopback development exposure if compatibility fails; never restore option injection, link-following publication, public auth downgrade or plaintext credential transport. Reopen affected issue dispositions after any rollback.

### Excluded

- Remote/public review-site hosting, authenticated reviewer service or remote-agent execution
- Changing real production configuration, rotating credentials, publishing packages or deploying software
- Implementing the 21 other-repository or 25 separately owned functional findings; security-relevant dependencies must be coordinated explicitly
